Class ConcatenatedOperationType

Direct Known Subclasses:
MLConcatenatedOperationType
public class ConcatenatedOperationType extends AbstractCoordinateOperationType
gml:ConcatenatedOperation is an ordered sequence of two or more coordinate operations. This sequence of operations is constrained by the requirement that the source coordinate reference system of step (n+1) must be the same as the target coordinate reference system of step (n). The source coordinate reference system of the first step and the target coordinate reference system of the last step are the source and target coordinate reference system associated with the concatenated operation. Instead of a forward operation, an inverse operation may be used for one or more of the operation steps mentioned above, if the inverse operation is uniquely defined by the forward operation. The gml:coordOperation property elements are an ordered sequence of associations to the two or more operations used by this concatenated operation. The AggregationAttributeGroup should be used to specify that the coordOperation associations are ordered.

Java class for ConcatenatedOperationType complex type.

The following schema fragment specifies the expected content contained within this class. 

 <complexType name="ConcatenatedOperationType">
   <complexContent>
     <extension base="{http://www.opengis.net/gml/3.2}AbstractCoordinateOperationType">
       <sequence>
         <element ref="{http://www.opengis.net/gml/3.2}coordOperation" maxOccurs="unbounded" minOccurs="2"/>
       </sequence>
       <attGroup ref="{http://www.opengis.net/gml/3.2}AggregationAttributeGroup"/>
     </extension>
   </complexContent>
 </complexType>

  • Method Details

    • getCoordOperations

      public List<jakarta.xml.bind.JAXBElement<CoordinateOperationPropertyType>> getCoordOperations()
      Gets the value of the coordOperations property.

      This accessor method returns a reference to the live list, not a snapshot. Therefore any modification you make to the returned list will be present inside the Jakarta XML Binding object. This is why there is not a set method for the coordOperations property.

      For example, to add a new item, do as follows: 

          getCoordOperations().add(newItem);

      Objects of the following type(s) are allowed in the list CoordOperation UsesOperation UsesSingleOperation
